body:
Implementation PRs for the vector pinning, to go with cashu-ts#786:

- CDK: cashubtc/cdk#2712 — pins the HTLC example proof (slot layout, receiver derivation at slots 1/2, spendability via both pathways), the V4 token decode/re-encode, and the wallet-level \sign_proofs\ derivation. The vector also caught a real interop bug: CDK was encoding \pe\ as a hex string on the CBOR path instead of a 33-byte bstr, so it could not decode spec-compliant P2BK V4 tokens (and vice versa); that is fixed in the PR.
- Nutshell: cashubtc/nutshell#1214 — pins the same vectors at the core, wallet (\_derive_p2bk_signing_keys\) and token layers. Receiver-side slot numbering was already correct there.

One spec-level observation while pinning the token byte-for-byte: the NUT-28 example V4 token orders the top-level CBOR map \m, u, t\, while the NUT-00 example tokens (pinned byte-for-byte by existing Nutshell tests) use \	, d, m, u\. CBOR maps are unordered so both decode everywhere, but the two test files are not byte-consistent with each other — may be worth aligning or stating key order is non-normative.

**minibits-cash:** So when minting onchain, cdk can present address that splices-in to fund your side of some channel? As of what I see now it's definitely onchain where the liquidity is short.

**thesimplekid:** Cdk but presets a normal onchain address user sends to (tx 1) then once received its does a splice (tx 2) and only issues the ecash after tx 2 and for amount minus fee of tx 2. It does require 2 txs and the user has to pay these so thats not the best. However, it does pass the fee burden onto the user in the most honest way as its the fee they force the mint to incur. 

This is similar to what fedimint now does, the federation only has 1 utxo so a user depositing sends to federation (tx 1) then federation consolidates into their 1 utxo (tx 2) and only issues ecash after tx 2 less the cost of the tx 2 fee.

**thesimplekid:** Users are depositing on chain and withdrawing via lighting or the reverse?

**minibits-cash:** Folks are withdrawing on onchain side. So the direction we'd need an incentive for is to mint onchain, or splice-out channels.

CBOR maps are unordered so both decode everywhere, but the two test files are not byte-consistent with each other — may be worth aligning or stating key order is non-normative.

Nice work @ye0man - and well worth it to squash that CDK bug!

Yes, map key order is non-normative, all three implementations do it differently and the spec has instances encoded from more than one.

Decoders MUST accept any order, and vector tests should compare decoded tokens, not bytes. I added a normative line to NUT-00 in this PR.

I've decided to close this PR that I made

I'm not against hashing the blinded outputs, and am happy for anyone else to advocate for this. It's just that I now have another solution ([Unpoisonable Blinded Outputs](https://gist.github.com/SatsAndSports/6c197ca9da984c1922483e74281d38db)) that fixes the poison issue directly, allowing us to keep using adverserial multi-party e-cash transactions (e.g. Spilman with non-interactive setup)
Folded into https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/404, which now carries `tests/14-test.md` with these vectors, the HTLC SIG_ALL case included.
